entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Ikrima ibn Abd Allah al-Barbari was a Muslim scholar of Berber descent, born in North Africa, who served as a mawla of the renowned Islamic scholar Ibn Abbas. He traveled extensively throughout the Islamic world, engaging in scholarly debates and literary pursuits. As a result, he became a prominent figure in the Islamic Golden Age, contributing to the development of Islamic theology and jurisprudence. His work had a lasting impact on the intellectual landscape of the Middle East and North Africa, shaping the theological debates of the Abbasid Caliphate. Through his writings, Ikrima ibn Abd Allah al-Barbari helped to codify the principles of Islamic law, ensuring the continued relevance of Ibn Abbas' teachings for generations to come.
